_description: Exhaustive inventory of Canadian electricity and natural gas utilities, by province/territory.
_methodology: Compiled from provincial regulator lists, utility association directories, and direct research. Includes both major distribution utilities and smaller municipal/cooperative utilities where identifiable.
_notes: This file is the project master reference for utility discovery. For provinces with many small utilities (especially Ontario with 60+ LDCs), only the largest are listed individually; the remainder are noted in the province-level notes field.

BC.name: British Columbia
BC.regulatory_notes: BCUC regulates rates for all investor-owned and most Crown utilities. BC Hydro rates are set via a government-directed process (often a Revenue Requirements Application to BCUC). FortisBC is fully BCUC-regulated. Municipal utilities set their own rates but may reference BC Hydro rates.
BC.market_structure: Vertically integrated Crown corporation (BC Hydro) dominates. FortisBC serves the southern interior for electricity and is the main gas distributor. Several small municipal electric utilities exist.

utilities.name: BC Hydro
utilities.service_area: Most of British Columbia (~95% of provincial electricity customers)
utilities.notes: Two-tier residential rate (Step 1 and Step 2). Rates set through Revenue Requirements Application to BCUC. Largest electric utility in BC.

utilities.name: FortisBC (Electric)
utilities.service_area: Southern interior BC including Kelowna, Trail, parts of Kootenay region (~180,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Subsidiary of Fortis Inc. Two-tier residential rate similar to BC Hydro but at different thresholds. Regulated by BCUC.

utilities.name: FortisBC Energy (Gas)
utilities.service_area: Most of British Columbia's natural gas customers (~1 million customers), including Lower Mainland, Interior, Vancouver Island, Whistler corridor
utilities.notes: Dominant gas distributor in BC. Quarterly commodity rate adjustments. Carbon tax applied on bills. Formerly Terasen Gas.

utilities.name: Nelson Hydro
utilities.service_area: City of Nelson and surrounding area in the West Kootenay region
utilities.notes: One of the oldest municipal electric utilities in BC. Generates own power from Bonnington Falls. Not regulated by BCUC; rates set by City Council.

utilities.name: New Westminster Electrical Utility
utilities.service_area: City of New Westminster
utilities.notes: Municipal utility purchasing wholesale power from BC Hydro. Rates set by City Council.

utilities.name: City of Penticton Electric Utility
utilities.service_area: City of Penticton
utilities.notes: Municipal utility purchasing wholesale power from FortisBC. Rates set by City Council.

utilities.name: City of Grand Forks Electrical Utility
utilities.service_area: City of Grand Forks
utilities.notes: Small municipal electric utility in the Boundary region. Purchases wholesale from FortisBC.

utilities.name: District of Summerland Electrical Utility
utilities.service_area: District of Summerland
utilities.notes: Municipal electric utility. Purchases wholesale from FortisBC. Irrigation is a significant customer class in the area.

AB.name: Alberta
AB.regulatory_notes: Alberta has a deregulated electricity market. The Alberta Electric System Operator (AESO) manages the wholesale power pool. Retail customers can choose a competitive retailer or stay on the Regulated Rate Option (RRO). Distribution (wires) is still regulated by AUC. Natural gas is similarly deregulated for retail, with regulated default supply.
AB.market_structure: Deregulated wholesale and retail electricity market. AESO pool price sets wholesale rates. Distribution remains regulated monopoly. RRO serves customers who do not choose a retailer. Gas distribution regulated; retail gas is competitive. Government has periodically imposed rate caps.

utilities.name: ENMAX
utilities.service_area: Calgary and surrounding area (electricity distribution and retail). Also competitive retail across Alberta.
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the City of Calgary. ENMAX Power Corporation handles distribution (regulated). ENMAX Energy handles competitive retail. Provides RRO for Calgary service area. Also offers natural gas retail.

utilities.name: EPCOR Distribution & Transmission
utilities.service_area: Edmonton and surrounding area (electricity distribution)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the City of Edmonton. EPCOR handles distribution in Edmonton. EPCOR Energy Services provides competitive retail. Regulated Rate Option provided for non-choosing customers.

utilities.name: ATCO Electric
utilities.service_area: Northern and east-central Alberta (approximately 265,000 customers in 245 communities)
utilities.notes: Part of Canadian Utilities (ATCO Group). Distribution and transmission utility. RRO provider for its service territory.

utilities.name: FortisAlberta
utilities.service_area: Central and southern Alberta (approximately 570,000 customers across 240 communities)
utilities.notes: Largest electricity distribution utility in Alberta by customer count. Distribution only (wires); does not sell energy. Subsidiary of Fortis Inc.

utilities.name: ATCO Gas
utilities.service_area: Most of Alberta outside Edmonton (approximately 1.2 million customers in more than 300 communities)
utilities.notes: Largest gas distributor in Alberta. Part of Canadian Utilities (ATCO Group). Distribution regulated by AUC. Retail gas is competitive; ATCO provides default supply.

utilities.name: EPCOR Natural Gas (formerly AltaGas Utilities)
utilities.service_area: Parts of Alberta including Airdrie, Cochrane, Leduc, and approximately 60 other communities
utilities.notes: EPCOR acquired AltaGas Utilities in 2020. Serves approximately 130,000 customers in smaller Alberta communities. Edmonton gas distribution is handled separately.

utilities.name: Direct Energy Regulated Services
utilities.service_area: RRO provider for ATCO Electric, ATCO Gas, and FortisAlberta service territories
utilities.notes: Provides the Regulated Rate Option (RRO) for customers in certain service territories who have not chosen a competitive retailer. Subsidiary of Centrica. Monthly RRO rate changes.

utilities.name: Rural Electrification Associations (REAs)
utilities.service_area: Various rural areas across Alberta (approximately 30+ REAs serving ~65,000 member-customers)
utilities.notes: There are approximately 30 REAs in Alberta. Each is a member-owned cooperative serving rural areas. They are distribution utilities regulated by AUC. Individually small; many have websites but rate info is inconsistent. Major ones include Battle River REA, Ermineskin REA, and others. Tracking each individually would require significant manual effort.

utilities.name: Alberta Electric System Operator (AESO)
utilities.service_area: Province-wide (wholesale market operator and transmission system operator, not a distribution utility)
utilities.notes: Not a retail utility. Independent system operator for the Alberta Interconnected Electric System. Manages the wholesale electricity pool price. Useful for tracking wholesale energy costs and pool price data that feeds into retail rates.

SK.name: Saskatchewan
SK.regulatory_notes: SaskPower and SaskEnergy are Crown corporations. Rates are reviewed by the Saskatchewan Rate Review Panel, which advises the government, but final rate approval is by the provincial cabinet via Order in Council. The panel's recommendations are not binding.
SK.market_structure: Vertically integrated Crown monopoly for both electricity (SaskPower) and gas (SaskEnergy). No retail competition.

utilities.name: SaskPower
utilities.service_area: Entire province of Saskatchewan (~545,000 customer accounts)
utilities.notes: Saskatchewan's sole electricity provider. Crown corporation. Rates set by government Order in Council after Rate Review Panel process. Generates, transmits, and distributes electricity across the province.

utilities.name: SaskEnergy
utilities.service_area: Province of Saskatchewan (~400,000 customer accounts)
utilities.notes: Saskatchewan's Crown natural gas distributor. Subsidiary TransGas handles transmission. Rates set by government Order in Council. Commodity charge adjusted periodically.

MB.name: Manitoba
MB.regulatory_notes: Manitoba Hydro applies to the PUB for rate changes. The PUB conducts public hearings and issues binding orders on rates. Centra Gas (a subsidiary of Manitoba Hydro) is also regulated by PUB for gas rates.
MB.market_structure: Vertically integrated Crown monopoly for both electricity and gas through Manitoba Hydro and its subsidiary Centra Gas. No retail competition. Manitoba benefits from very low-cost hydroelectric generation.

utilities.name: Manitoba Hydro
utilities.service_area: Entire province of Manitoba for electricity (~590,000 electric customers, ~285,000 gas customers via Centra Gas subsidiary)
utilities.notes: Crown corporation providing both electricity and natural gas (via Centra Gas subsidiary). Has some of the lowest electricity rates in North America due to extensive hydroelectric resources. Gas commodity rates adjusted quarterly.

ON.name: Ontario
ON.regulatory_notes: OEB regulates all electricity Local Distribution Companies (LDCs) and natural gas distributors. Electricity rates have multiple components: commodity (set via RPP or HOEP), delivery, regulatory charges, and Global Adjustment. Time-of-Use (TOU) pricing is standard for residential customers with smart meters. The OEB also sets the Ontario Electricity Rebate.
ON.market_structure: Hybrid market: generation is competitive (IESO-managed), but distribution is regulated monopoly through 60+ LDCs. Residential customers are mostly on Regulated Price Plan (RPP) with Time-of-Use or tiered rates. Large consumers can participate in wholesale market. Gas distribution is a regulated monopoly (Enbridge Gas).
ON.total_electricity_ldcs: Approximately 60 local distribution companies (LDCs) exist in Ontario. The top 15-20 by customer count are listed individually below.

utilities.name: Hydro One Networks
utilities.service_area: Rural and small-town Ontario, plus transmission across the province (~1.4 million distribution customers)
utilities.notes: Largest electricity distributor in Ontario by service area. Formerly Crown-owned, now publicly traded (majority Ontario government ownership). Also operates the provincial high-voltage transmission grid. Multiple rate zones (e.g., Hydro One Networks, Hydro One Remote Communities).

utilities.name: Toronto Hydro-Electric System
utilities.service_area: City of Toronto (~780,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Largest municipal LDC in Ontario by customer count. Wholly owned by the City of Toronto. Distribution only; commodity charges set by OEB/IESO.

utilities.name: Alectra Utilities
utilities.service_area: Greater Hamilton, Mississauga, Brampton, St. Catharines, Vaughan, Markham, and surrounding areas (~1 million customers)
utilities.notes: Formed from merger of Horizon Utilities, PowerStream, Enersource, and Hydro One Brampton in 2017. Second-largest municipal LDC in Ontario. Multiple rate zones from the merged utilities.

utilities.name: Hydro Ottawa
utilities.service_area: City of Ottawa and surrounding area (~345,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the City of Ottawa. Third-largest LDC by customer count.

utilities.name: London Hydro
utilities.service_area: City of London (~160,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the City of London.

utilities.name: Oshawa PUC Networks
utilities.service_area: City of Oshawa (~58,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the City of Oshawa.

utilities.name: Kitchener-Wilmot Hydro
utilities.service_area: Cities of Kitchener and Wilmot Township (~95,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Owned by the City of Kitchener and Township of Wilmot.

utilities.name: Waterloo North Hydro
utilities.service_area: City of Waterloo, Township of Woolwich, and Township of Wellesley (~58,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Jointly owned by the municipalities it serves.

utilities.name: Thunder Bay Hydro
utilities.service_area: City of Thunder Bay (~50,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the City of Thunder Bay. Northwestern Ontario.

utilities.name: Greater Sudbury Hydro
utilities.service_area: City of Greater Sudbury (~48,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the City of Greater Sudbury.

utilities.name: Oakville Hydro Electricity Distribution
utilities.service_area: Town of Oakville (~72,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the Town of Oakville.

utilities.name: Burlington Hydro
utilities.service_area: City of Burlington (~68,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the City of Burlington.

utilities.name: Milton Hydro Distribution
utilities.service_area: Town of Milton (~38,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the Town of Milton. Growing service area.

utilities.name: Halton Hills Hydro
utilities.service_area: Town of Halton Hills including Georgetown and Acton (~22,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Wholly owned by the Town of Halton Hills.

utilities.name: Guelph Hydro Electric Systems (now Alectra)
utilities.service_area: City of Guelph (~52,000 customers, now served under Alectra Utilities)
utilities.notes: Guelph Hydro merged into Alectra Utilities. Rates may still be listed under a separate Guelph rate zone at OEB.

utilities.name: Cambridge and North Dumfries Hydro
utilities.service_area: City of Cambridge and Township of North Dumfries (~58,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Owned by the City of Cambridge and Township of North Dumfries.

utilities.name: Ottawa River Power Corporation
utilities.service_area: Parts of the Ottawa Valley (~12,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Smaller LDC serving communities along the Ottawa River.

utilities.name: Enbridge Gas Inc.
utilities.service_area: Most of Ontario (~3.8 million customers). Formed from merger of Enbridge Gas Distribution and Union Gas.
utilities.notes: Dominant natural gas distributor in Ontario. Formed from 2019 merger of Enbridge Gas Distribution (southern Ontario) and Union Gas (northern and southwestern Ontario). Two legacy rate zones still in effect. Quarterly commodity rate adjustments. OEB-regulated.

utilities.name: Independent Electricity System Operator (IESO)
utilities.service_area: Province-wide (wholesale market operator, not a distribution utility)
utilities.notes: Not a retail utility. Operates Ontario's wholesale electricity market and manages the provincial power grid. Publishes the Hourly Ontario Energy Price (HOEP) and Global Adjustment data. Key data source for understanding Ontario electricity commodity costs.

QC.name: Quebec
QC.regulatory_notes: Hydro-Quebec Distribution rates are set by the Regie de l'energie. Quebec benefits from a heritage pool of low-cost hydroelectric generation; the first block of electricity (heritage pool) is priced at a legislated ceiling, and supply above that is procured competitively. Energir (gas) is also regulated by the Regie.
QC.market_structure: Vertically integrated Crown monopoly (Hydro-Quebec) dominates electricity. Heritage pool pricing keeps residential rates among the lowest in North America. Nine municipal distributors exist but serve a small fraction of customers. Energir is the main gas distributor.
QC.municipal_distributors_note: Quebec has 9 municipally owned electricity distribution systems (cooperatives or municipal utilities). These are small and serve specific towns. They purchase power from Hydro-Quebec at wholesale rates and set their own distribution charges.

utilities.name: Hydro-Quebec
utilities.service_area: Virtually all of Quebec (~4.4 million customers, serving ~99% of the province's electricity needs)
utilities.notes: Largest electric utility in Canada. Crown corporation. Rates are among the lowest in North America due to extensive hydroelectric resources (heritage pool). Two-tier residential rate (Rate D). Large industrial customers on Rate L. Regulated by the Regie de l'energie.

utilities.name: Energir (formerly Gaz Metro)
utilities.service_area: Southern Quebec, primarily Greater Montreal region and parts of southern Quebec (~210,000 gas customers)
utilities.notes: Formerly Gaz Metro. Main natural gas distributor in Quebec. Regulated by the Regie de l'energie. Also expanding into renewable natural gas (RNG). Relatively small customer base compared to electricity because Quebec heating is predominantly electric.

utilities.name: Hydro-Sherbrooke
utilities.service_area: City of Sherbrooke (~85,000 customers)
utilities.notes: One of 9 municipal electricity distributors in Quebec. Purchases wholesale power from Hydro-Quebec. Rates set by City Council.

utilities.name: Hydro-Joliette
utilities.service_area: City of Joliette
utilities.notes: One of 9 municipal electricity distributors in Quebec. Small service area.

utilities.name: Electricite de Coaticook
utilities.service_area: Town of Coaticook
utilities.notes: One of 9 municipal electricity distributors in Quebec.

utilities.name: Electricite de Magog
utilities.service_area: City of Magog
utilities.notes: One of 9 municipal electricity distributors in Quebec.

utilities.name: Westmount Hydro
utilities.service_area: City of Westmount (on the Island of Montreal)
utilities.notes: One of 9 municipal electricity distributors in Quebec. Small affluent municipality on the Island of Montreal.

utilities.name: Other Quebec Municipal Distributors
utilities.service_area: Alma, Amos, Baie-Comeau, and Saguenay area cooperatives
utilities.notes: Remaining municipal distributors in Quebec. Small operations. Rate data is difficult to find online. Collectively serve a very small percentage of Quebec electricity customers.

NB.name: New Brunswick
NB.electricity_regulator: New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board (NBEUB)
NB.gas_regulator: New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board (NBEUB)
NB.regulatory_notes: NB Power rates are regulated by the NBEUB. Liberty Utilities (gas) is also regulated by the NBEUB. Electricity rates in NB are moderate; the province uses a mix of hydro, nuclear (Point Lepreau), and thermal generation.
NB.market_structure: Vertically integrated Crown corporation (NB Power) for electricity. Limited natural gas penetration (Liberty Utilities serves parts of southern NB). No retail electricity competition.

utilities.name: NB Power (New Brunswick Power Corporation)
utilities.service_area: Entire province of New Brunswick (~400,000 direct and indirect customers)
utilities.notes: Crown corporation. Vertically integrated (generation, transmission, distribution). Mix of hydro, nuclear (Point Lepreau), and thermal generation. Some municipal utilities (like Saint John Energy and Edmundston) distribute NB Power electricity.

utilities.name: Saint John Energy
utilities.service_area: City of Saint John (~36,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Municipal utility distributing electricity in Saint John. Purchases wholesale from NB Power.

utilities.name: Edmundston (Energie Edmundston)
utilities.service_area: City of Edmundston (~8,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Municipal utility in Edmundston. Has some own generation capacity. Bilingual (English/French) service area.

utilities.name: Perth-Andover Electric Light Commission
utilities.service_area: Village of Perth-Andover
utilities.notes: Very small municipal electric utility.

utilities.name: Liberty Utilities (Gas New Brunswick)
utilities.service_area: Parts of southern New Brunswick including Saint John, Moncton, Fredericton (~12,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Formerly Enbridge Gas New Brunswick. Subsidiary of Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp (Liberty). Natural gas penetration in NB is limited. Regulated by NBEUB.

NS.name: Nova Scotia
NS.electricity_regulator: Nova Scotia Utility and Review Board (NSUARB)
NS.gas_regulator: Nova Scotia Utility and Review Board (NSUARB)
NS.regulatory_notes: Nova Scotia Power (NSPI) rates are regulated by the NSUARB through general rate applications. Heritage Gas is also NSUARB-regulated. Nova Scotia has been transitioning away from coal toward renewables and natural gas.
NS.market_structure: Investor-owned utility (Nova Scotia Power, subsidiary of Emera) holds a vertically integrated monopoly on electricity. Limited natural gas distribution through Heritage Gas. No retail electricity competition.

utilities.name: Nova Scotia Power (NSPI)
utilities.service_area: Entire province of Nova Scotia (~530,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Subsidiary of Emera Inc. Vertically integrated (generation, transmission, distribution). Historically coal-dependent; transitioning to renewables. Subject to renewable portfolio standards. Fuel Adjustment Mechanism adjusts rates for fuel cost changes.

utilities.name: Heritage Gas
utilities.service_area: Halifax Regional Municipality, parts of Dartmouth and surrounding areas
utilities.notes: Only natural gas distributor in Nova Scotia. Relatively small customer base as gas distribution infrastructure is limited. Uses gas from the Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline (Sable Island and imported LNG). Regulated by NSUARB.

PE.name: Prince Edward Island
PE.regulatory_notes: Maritime Electric rates are regulated by IRAC. PEI has limited gas infrastructure; no piped natural gas distribution utility. The province imports most of its electricity via submarine cables from New Brunswick and has growing wind generation.
PE.market_structure: Single investor-owned electric utility (Maritime Electric). No natural gas distribution utility. PEI is heavily dependent on imported electricity from NB and wind power. Province has ambitious renewable energy targets.

utilities.name: Maritime Electric
utilities.service_area: Entire province of Prince Edward Island (~86,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Subsidiary of Fortis Inc. Sole electric utility on PEI. Imports most power from NB via submarine cables. Has growing on-island wind generation. Energy Cost Adjustment Mechanism (ECAM) adjusts rates for fuel and purchased power costs.

utilities.name: PEI Energy Corporation
utilities.service_area: Province-wide (wind generation and energy policy, not a distribution utility)
utilities.notes: Crown corporation involved in energy policy and wind farm development. Not a distribution utility. Sells wind power to Maritime Electric under contract.

NL.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
NL.electricity_regulator: Board of Commissioners of Public Utilities (PUB NL)
NL.regulatory_notes: Newfoundland Power and NL Hydro rates are regulated by the PUB. The province has no piped natural gas distribution system. The Muskrat Falls hydroelectric project has significantly impacted rate discussions, with the provincial government implementing rate mitigation measures.
NL.market_structure: NL Hydro (Crown) generates and transmits; Newfoundland Power (Fortis subsidiary, investor-owned) distributes to most of the island. NL Hydro also serves isolated rural/diesel communities directly. No natural gas distribution. Muskrat Falls cost overruns have created significant rate pressure.

utilities.name: Newfoundland Power
utilities.service_area: Most of the Island of Newfoundland (~270,000 customers, approximately 87% of island customers)
utilities.notes: Subsidiary of Fortis Inc. Distributes electricity on the Island of Newfoundland. Purchases most power from NL Hydro. Regulated by PUB NL.

utilities.name: Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro (NL Hydro)
utilities.service_area: Labrador and isolated communities in Newfoundland (~35,000 direct customers). Also generates/transmits power for the entire province.
utilities.notes: Crown corporation (subsidiary of Nalcor Energy, now NL Hydro). Generates and transmits electricity province-wide. Directly serves customers in Labrador and isolated rural communities (many diesel-powered). Muskrat Falls project owner. Isolated diesel communities have higher rates that are cross-subsidized.

YT.name: Yukon
YT.regulatory_notes: Both Yukon Energy and ATCO Electric Yukon are regulated by the YUB. No piped natural gas distribution in Yukon (heating oil and propane are common alternatives). The Yukon government subsidizes electricity costs to keep rates manageable.
YT.market_structure: Two-utility system: Yukon Energy (Crown) generates and transmits; ATCO Electric Yukon distributes to most customers. No natural gas distribution utility. Hydro-based generation supplemented by diesel and LNG in winter peak periods.

utilities.name: Yukon Energy Corporation
utilities.service_area: Yukon-wide generation and transmission. Direct retail service to some industrial customers and communities.
utilities.notes: Crown corporation responsible for generation and transmission. Sells wholesale power to ATCO Electric Yukon for distribution. Also directly serves some large industrial customers. Hydro-dominant with diesel backup.

utilities.name: ATCO Electric Yukon (formerly Yukon Electrical Company)
utilities.service_area: Whitehorse and most Yukon communities (~19,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Subsidiary of ATCO Ltd. (Canadian Utilities). Distribution utility for most Yukon retail customers. Purchases wholesale from Yukon Energy. Formerly Yukon Electrical Company Limited.

NT.name: Northwest Territories
NT.electricity_regulator: Northwest Territories Public Utilities Board (NT PUB)
NT.regulatory_notes: NTPC rates are regulated by the NT PUB. Rates vary significantly by community due to different generation sources (hydro vs. diesel). There is a Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP) that subsidizes rates in higher-cost communities. No piped natural gas distribution utility (some communities use trucked propane or heating oil).
NT.market_structure: Single Crown utility (NTPC) serves the entire territory. Large rate differentials between hydro-served and diesel-served communities. Government subsidies help equalize rates across communities.

utilities.name: Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC)
utilities.service_area: All communities in the Northwest Territories (~22,000 customers across 33 communities)
utilities.notes: Crown corporation. Sole electricity provider in the NWT. Mix of hydro (Snare, Taltson, Bluefish systems) and diesel generation depending on community. Rates vary by zone: hydro communities pay less, diesel communities pay more. TPSP subsidy helps equalize rates.

utilities.name: Northland Utilities (NWT)
utilities.service_area: Yellowknife and Hay River (~8,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Subsidiary of ATCO. Distributes electricity in Yellowknife and Hay River, purchasing wholesale from NTPC. Regulated by the NT PUB.

NU.name: Nunavut
NU.electricity_regulator: Utility Rates Review Council of Nunavut (URRC)
NU.regulatory_notes: QEC rates are reviewed by the URRC, but final rate approval is by the Government of Nunavut. There is no piped natural gas infrastructure anywhere in Nunavut. All communities rely on diesel generation for electricity and heating oil for heat. Government subsidizes electricity costs substantially.
NU.market_structure: Single Crown utility (QEC) serves all 25 communities. 100% diesel generation. Extremely high cost of electricity. Government provides substantial subsidies to keep customer rates manageable. No natural gas infrastructure exists.

utilities.name: Qulliq Energy Corporation (QEC)
utilities.service_area: All 25 communities in Nunavut (~16,000 customers)
utilities.notes: Crown corporation. Sole electricity provider in Nunavut. 100% diesel generation in all 25 communities. No interconnection to any other grid. Fuel must be shipped in by sealift or air, making costs extremely high. Government subsidizes a significant portion of actual costs. Each community has its own standalone diesel plant. No piped natural gas exists anywhere in Nunavut.
